note: Willim et al. (2024) describe 33 individuals with LRRC7-related disorder where hyperphagia-associated obesity is present in a subset of cases rather than universally.

evidence.text: In a primary cohort of 33 individuals with dominant LRRC7 variants, hyperphagia-associated obesity was reported in several cases rather than across the entire cohort, including 4 of 14 cases with truncating variants.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors
source.quote: We identify here 33 individuals (one of them previously described) with a dominant neurodevelopmental disorder due to heterozygous missense or loss-of-function variants in LRRC7. The clinical spectrum involves intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression and, in several cases, hyperphagia-associated obesity.

numbers.metric: truncating variant cases evaluated for hyperphagia
